summary: NSW (Australia) manslaughter (reckless/negligent, no intent to kill) actual sentences for 80 imprisoned adults had a mean head sentence of 8 years (range 3-16) and a mean non-parole period of 5.3 years (range 1.5-12).
harm_duration: 8 years mean head sentence (range 3-16); 5.3 years mean non-parole period (range 1.5-12)
label_raw: Manslaughter, actual sentences imposed (max 25 years; NSW Sentencing Council Homicide report)
source_citation: NSW Sentencing Council, Homicide report, May 2021, https://sentencingcouncil.nsw.gov.au/content/dam/dcj/sentencing-council/documents/our-work/homicide/homicide-report.pdf

summary: NSW (Australia) actual murder sentences in the 20-year SNPP cohort (80 of 85 adults, excluding 5 life) had a mean head sentence of 25.6 years and a mean non-parole period of 18.9 years.
harm_duration: 25.6 years mean head sentence; 18.9 years mean non-parole period
label_raw: Murder, actual sentences imposed (NSW Sentencing Council Homicide report)
source_citation: NSW Sentencing Council, Homicide report, May 2021, https://sentencingcouncil.nsw.gov.au/content/dam/dcj/sentencing-council/documents/our-work/homicide/homicide-report.pdf

summary: NSW (Australia) murder (intentional or reckless indifference to human life) carries a standard non-parole period of 20 years, rising to 25 years where the victim is a child or certain public officials.
harm_duration: 20 years (standard non-parole period; 25 years for child/public-official victims)
label_raw: Murder, SNPP (Crimes Act 1900 (NSW) s. 19A; Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999 s. 54D)
source_citation: Crimes Act 1900 (NSW) s. 19A; Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999 (NSW) Table to s. 54D; NSW Judicial Commission Sentencing Bench Book 'Murder' https://www.judcom.nsw.gov.au/publications/benchbks/sentencing/murder.html

summary: Canada first-degree (planned and deliberate, intentional) murder carries mandatory life imprisonment with a fixed 25-year parole-ineligibility period.
source_citation: Criminal Code of Canada, RSC 1985 c. C-46, ss. 235, 745(a); Justice Laws Website https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-46/section-745.html; Public Safety Canada, Sentence Calculation Fast Facts (2021)

summary: Canada manslaughter (reckless/negligent unlawful-act homicide, no intent to kill) has no general mandatory minimum and, where a life sentence is imposed, parole eligibility arises at 7 years.
harm_duration: 7 years (parole-eligibility floor where life imposed; extendable to 10 under s. 743.6)
source_citation: Criminal Code of Canada, RSC 1985 c. C-46, s. 236; https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-46/section-236.html

summary: Canada second-degree (intentional but not planned) murder carries mandatory life imprisonment with a judge-set parole-ineligibility period of 10 to 25 years (default 10).
source_citation: Criminal Code of Canada, RSC 1985 c. C-46, ss. 745(c), 745.4; https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-46/section-745.html

summary: India murder under IPC s. 302 (intent to kill, or intent to cause injury sufficient in the ordinary course to cause death) is punishable by death or life imprisonment plus fine, with life the standard and death reserved for the rarest of rare cases.
harm_duration: life imprisonment (or death penalty in rarest-of-rare cases)
label_raw: Murder, IPC s. 302 (re-enacted as BNS 2023 s. 103)
source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 302; India Code https://www.indiacode.nic.in/; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 s. 103; analysis https://thelegalschool.in/blog/difference-between-302-and-304-ipc

summary: India culpable homicide not amounting to murder under IPC s. 304 Part I (act done with intention or knowledge of likely death) is punishable by life imprisonment or up to 10 years plus fine.
harm_duration: life imprisonment, or up to 10 years (statutory maximum)
label_raw: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s. 304 Part I (BNS 2023 s. 105)
source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 304 Part I; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/show-data?actid=AC_CEN_5_23_00037_186045_1523266765688&orderno=341; BNS 2023 s. 105

summary: India culpable homicide not amounting to murder under IPC s. 304 Part II (knowledge act is likely to cause death but no intention) is punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment, or fine, or both.
harm_duration: up to 10 years (statutory maximum; no life)
label_raw: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s. 304 Part II
source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 304 Part II; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/show-data?actid=AC_CEN_5_23_00037_186045_1523266765688&orderno=341

summary: Ireland manslaughter (unlawful act or gross negligence, no intent to kill) has no mandatory minimum and a maximum of life, with a typical custodial range cited at roughly 4 to 15 years.
harm_duration: ~4 to 15 years (indicative typical custodial range; no formal guideline)
source_citation: Judicial Council Sentencing Guidelines & Information Committee materials, https://judicialcouncil.ie/assets/uploads/Sentence%20Information%20the%20General%20Public.pdf (practitioner/secondary characterization, indicative only)

summary: Ireland murder (intentional killing or intent to cause serious injury) carries mandatory life imprisonment, with parole eligibility after 12 years and average time actually served on a life sentence of about 20 years.
harm_duration: ~20 years average time served (parole eligibility after 12 years)
source_citation: Criminal Justice Act 1990 (Ireland), s. 2; Parole Act 2019; Law Reform Commission Mandatory Sentences (LRC 108-2013); 'Life imprisonment in Ireland', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_imprisonment_in_Ireland

summary: New Zealand aggravated murder (s. 104 list, e.g. high brutality or multiple victims) requires a minimum non-parole period of 17 years unless manifestly unjust.
source_citation: Sentencing Act 2002 (NZ) s. 104; R v Williams [2005] 2 NZLR 506 (CA); https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2002/0009/latest/DLM136497.html

summary: New Zealand manslaughter (no murderous intent, unlawful act or gross negligence) has a maximum of life imprisonment but life is optional, with no statutory minimum and determinate terms usual.
harm_duration: no statutory minimum; determinate terms usual (max life)
source_citation: Crimes Act 1961 (NZ) s. 177; NZ Law Commission R139 ch. 11 'Sentencing for manslaughter', https://www.lawcom.govt.nz/sites/html-pubs/r139/Chapter+11+-+Sentencing+for+homicide/Sentencing+for+manslaughter.html

summary: New Zealand murder (intentional, or reckless knowing death likely) carries a presumption of life imprisonment with a default minimum period of imprisonment of 10 years before parole.
harm_duration: 10 years (default minimum period of imprisonment before parole)

summary: Scotland culpable homicide (lacks the wicked intent/recklessness of murder, analogous to manslaughter) attracts determinate terms, with 16 offenders receiving an average sentence of about 7 years (2,589 days) in 2021-22.
harm_duration: ~7 years (2,589 days) average determinate sentence in 2021-22
label_raw: Culpable homicide, determinate sentences (Scots common law)
source_citation: Scottish Government, Criminal Proceedings in Scotland 2021-22, custodial sentences by type of crime, https://www.gov.scot/publications/criminal-proceedings-scotland-2021-22/pages/13/

summary: Scotland murder (intent to kill or wicked recklessness) carries mandatory life imprisonment, with an average punishment part of 20.5 years for life sentences in 2023-24.
harm_duration: 20.5 years average punishment part (parole floor) in 2023-24
label_raw: Murder, mandatory life with punishment part (Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 s. 205)
source_citation: Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 s. 205; Scottish Government, Criminal Proceedings in Scotland 2023-24, Appendix on punishment part of life sentences and OLRs, https://www.gov.scot/publications/criminal-proceedings-in-scotland-2023-24/pages/appendix-length-of-the-punishment-part-of-life-sentences-and-olrs/
